thread:
Ravi: FYI seeing p95/p99 east-west latency blips during the 09:00 batching ramp. Affected flows mostly between gpu-node-12 -> gpu-node-45. Anyone else?
Sasha: Yup, dashboards show latency jumping from ~1ms to 20-35ms for short windows. Correlates with batcher ramp (lots of new short TCP connections).
Ben: I'm capturing packets now on node45. Early look shows a fair amount of out-of-order segments and occasional RSTs.
Ben: ```
12:08:59.543210 IP gpu-node-12.35101 > gpu-node-45.52000: Flags [P.], seq 1001:1056, ack 2001, length 55 (out-of-order)
12:08:59.543400 IP gpu-node-12.35102 > gpu-node-45.52000: Flags [P.], seq 1056:1108, ack 2001, length 52
```
Sasha: that pattern + bursts of SYNs suggests reordering rather than outright drops. Also seeing a spike in short-lived TCP flows in netflow.
infra-bot: netflow-summary: ~140k new ephemeral flows from service `batcher.backend` between 09:02-09:06; src ports clustered in 35000-35999.
Nina: Checked ToR counters — ECMP group for that pod shows hash_flips and some queue microbursts. Sample: `hash_flips=942, queue_full_events=7, drops=2`.
Ravi: sounds like ECMP path-churn + microbursts could cause packets for the same 5-tuple to arrive on different paths (OOO). If the batcher opens many connections, source ports bounce and may change per flow, making L4 hashing unstable.
Ben: NIC stats on node45 look OK (no rx_errors), but kernel softirq backlog did spike. dmesg shows "softirq: net_rx blocked Xs" around the same time. CPU scheduling may delay RX processing and worsen reordering symptoms.
Sasha: Also vendor logs indicate microburst shaping hit some egress ports during ramp. Combination of shaping and ECMP changes = OOO.
Ravi: mitigation candidates: 1) make batcher reuse connections (persistent pooling), 2) smooth flow arrival (throttle ramp), 3) enable sticky L4-hash / flowlet-aware hashing on ToR.
Ben: quick test: enabled keepalive/persistent Session in a small canary and OOO counts dropped significantly. Also tried a synthetic workload that reuses a single flow, near-zero reorders.
Sasha: we measured p99: baseline ~30ms during peak, canary with persistent connections ~5-7ms. Promising.
infra-bot: perf-note: enabling persistent connections for 40% of traffic in staging reduced p95 by ~55% during the test window.
Nina: Vendor can enable sticky L4 hashing on ECMP groups, but it needs a config push and ~15m maintenance window. Low risk per vendor.
Ravi: short-term actions for today's window: - throttle batcher ramp by ~25% to spread new-flow arrival - increase NIC and kernel RX processing capacity on hot nodes (RPS/RFS adjustments) - deploy a small change to batcher to enable connection pooling behind a flag.
Ben: commands we tested on node45: ```# turn up RPS
echo f > /sys/class/net/eth0/queues/rx-0/rps_cpus
# python client quick patch
s = requests.Session()
s.mount('http://', HTTPAdapter(pool_maxsize=60))
```
Sasha: after throttling ramp by 25% and rolling the keepalive canary, p99 during the next window dropped from 32ms -> 6ms. We'll add panels for new_flow_rate, ecmp_hash_flips, ooo_packet_count.
Nina: I've scheduled the ToR sticky-hash change for 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC; vendor will apply and we can validate across 3 peak windows before closing.
Ravi: owners: Ben - add connection pool PR & runtime flag (PR by EOD). Nina - coordinate ToR config change and vendor sign-off. Sasha - add canary and dashboards. I'll follow up on throttling defaults.
Ben: opening INF ticket and PR, adding fallback single-conn mode.
infra-bot: incident INF-3298 created with attached telemetry and initial actions.
Ravi: Good work. Let's monitor next 3 peak windows post-change before we fully close. :thumbsup:
